title: The Evil of Wealth Without Enjoyment

questions.question: There is an evil that I have seen under the sun, and it lies heavy on whom?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:1 (ESV): "There is an evil that I have seen under the sun, and it lies heavy on mankind:"

questions.question: God gives wealth, possessions, and honor, so that he lacks nothing... yet God does not give him power to do what?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:2 (ESV): "yet God does not give him power to enjoy them,"

questions.question: If a man fathers a hundred children and lives many years... but his soul is not satisfied with life's good things... a stillborn child is what?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:3 (ESV): "I say that a stillborn child is better off than he."

questions.question: All the toil of man is for his mouth, yet his appetite is not what?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:7 (ESV): "yet his appetite is not satisfied."

questions.question: For who knows what is good for man while he lives the few days of his... life?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:12 (ESV): "while he lives the few days of his vain life,"

questions.question: For it comes in vanity and goes in darkness, and in darkness its name is what?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:4 (ESV): "and in darkness its name is covered."

questions.question: Moreover, it has not seen the sun or known anything, yet it finds rest rather than whom?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:5 (ESV): "yet it finds rest rather than he."

questions.question: Even though he should live a thousand years twice over, yet enjoy no good—do not all go to one what?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:6 (ESV): "do not all go to one place?"

questions.question: For what advantage has the wise man over the what?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:8 (ESV): "For what advantage has the wise man over the fool?"

questions.question: Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the what?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:9 (ESV): "Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the appetite."

questions.question: Whatever has come to be has already been named, and it is known what... is?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:10 (ESV): "and it is known what man is,"

questions.question: And that he is not able to dispute with one stronger than whom?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:10 (ESV): "and that he is not able to dispute with one stronger than he."

questions.question: The more words, the more vanity, and what is the advantage to whom?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:11 (ESV): "and what is the advantage to man?"

questions.question: For who can tell man what will be after him under the what?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:12 (ESV): "For who can tell man what will be after him under the sun?"

questions.question: This also is vanity; it is a grievous what?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:2 (ESV): "This is vanity; it is a grievous evil."

key_verse_text: All the toil of man is for his mouth, yet his appetite is not satisfied.
